claim: Caenorhabditis elegans forms a memory of particular foods after experience
source_text: Here, we show that the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans forms a memory of particular foods after experience and displays behavioral plasticity, increasing the feeding response when they subsequently recognize the familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental observations showing differential feeding responses to familiar vs novel bacteria across multiple assays (Figures 1-3).

claim: C. elegans displays behavioral plasticity by increasing the feeding response when they recognize familiar food
source_text: Here, we show that the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans forms a memory of particular foods after experience and displays behavioral plasticity, increasing the feeding response when they subsequently recognize the familiar food.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through feeding rate measurements showing higher pumping rates on familiar bacteria compared to novel bacteria (Figures 1B-E, 2B-E).

claim: Recognition of familiar food activates the pair of ADF chemosensory neurons
source_text: We found that recognition of familiar food activates the pair of ADF chemosensory neurons, which subsequently increase serotonin release.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by calcium imaging data showing ADF activation in response to familiar but not novel bacteria (Figure 12).

claim: ADF chemosensory neurons increase serotonin release in response to familiar food
source_text: We found that recognition of familiar food activates the pair of ADF chemosensory neurons, which subsequently increase serotonin release.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by immunohistochemistry showing increased serotonin-positive uptaking cells when animals are exposed to familiar food (Figure 11D).

claim: Released serotonin activates the feeding response mainly by acting humorally
source_text: The released serotonin activates the feeding response mainly by acting humorally and directly activates SER-7, a type 7 serotonin receptor, in MC motor neurons in the feeding organ.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the fact that serotonin from extrapharyngeal ADF neurons affects pharyngeal MC neurons, and NSM neurons within the pharynx do not contribute to this response (Figure 8).

claim: Serotonin directly activates SER-7, a type 7 serotonin receptor, in MC motor neurons in the feeding organ
source_text: The released serotonin activates the feeding response mainly by acting humorally and directly activates SER-7, a type 7 serotonin receptor, in MC motor neurons in the feeding organ.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by rescue experiments showing that SER-7 expression in MC neurons restores feeding response (Figure 8E,F).

claim: Worms sense the taste and/or smell of novel bacteria, which overrides the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria on feeding
source_text: Our data suggest that worms sense the taste and/or smell of novel bacteria, which overrides the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria on feeding by suppressing the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experiments with conditioned media showing that soluble cues from novel bacteria suppress feeding (Figure 14), combined with calcium imaging showing ADF is not activated by novel bacteria.

claim: Novel bacteria suppress feeding by suppressing the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons
source_text: Our data suggest that worms sense the taste and/or smell of novel bacteria, which overrides the stimulatory effect of familiar bacteria on feeding by suppressing the activity of ADF or its upstream neurons.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from calcium imaging showing ADF is not activated by novel bacteria and conditioned media experiments showing suppression of feeding response.
